info.name: Harava Platform API
info.description:
Harava Insights multi-tenant financial platform. Folders cover platform admin, auth, account, staff invitations, user management, MFA, companies, insights, QuickBooks connect, the mirrored QuickBooks data read API (per-entity: accounts, invoices, bills, …), the client portal, and reference data (timezones, countries with currency + timezones, currencies).

Companies are created by connecting QuickBooks (folder 'QuickBooks (firm console)' -> 'Add Company (start OAuth)'); there is no manual create-company endpoint. Once connected, a backfill job pulls all QuickBooks data into Harava's own tables and CDC keeps it fresh; read it via 'QuickBooks Data (firm console)' or the portal equivalents.

Login/accept requests capture tokens into collection variables automatically. DPoP: a collection-level pre-request script auto-attaches a `DPoP` proof to every request (jsrsasign, loaded once from CDN and cached in `jsrsasignSrc`). Required when the server has harava.dpop.enabled=true; harmless when false.

item.name: 1. Platform Admin

request.description:
Creates the tenant and emails the owner an invitation. Copy the invite token from the email into {{inviteToken}}.

billingMode is optional and defaults to SUBSCRIPTION when omitted — set {{billingMode}} to OPEN for a tenant that is not subject to paid billing. countryCode (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), defaultCurrency (ISO 4217), and timezone (IANA) are the firm's optional display defaults; remove them to omit.

item.description: Platform control plane. Onboard and manage tenants (firms).

item.name: 2. Owner Onboarding
item.description: Owner arrives by invitation only, sets a password, and is signed in.

item.name: 3. Tenant Auth

request.description: Resolves a workspace subdomain to its tenantId and display name. Returns 404 if the subdomain is unknown or the tenant is suspended. Clients call this on the login screen, then send the returned tenantId as the X-Tenant-ID header on /auth/login.

item.description: Tenant user authentication, MFA, and password recovery.

item.name: 6. Users (owner/admin)

request.description: All fields optional. role accepts ADMIN or MEMBER; enabled=false blocks login and revokes sessions.

item.description: Owner/Admin management of the tenant's staff users (/api/v1/account/users).

request.description: Sends a fresh email OTP to the signed-in user (only works while EMAIL MFA is active). Use this before 'Disable MFA' when switching to the authenticator: send the code, read it from your email (or MailHog), then put it in {{mfaCode}} and call Disable MFA.

Enables SMS MFA. Requires a phone number on the account (collected at invite acceptance). Stubbed until Twilio is wired up: no real SMS is sent and the login SMS challenge is satisfied by the configured static code (SMS_STUB_CODE, default 123456).
Sends a fresh SMS OTP to the signed-in user (only works while SMS MFA is active). While stubbed, nothing is delivered — just pass the static stub code (default 123456) as {{mfaCode}}.
Disables MFA. Requires a current second-factor code in {{mfaCode}}: a live TOTP code, a fresh email OTP (use 'Send email OTP (step-up)' first), or a backup code.

item.name: 8. Companies (firm console)

request.description: Invite a portal viewer to this company. Repeat for any number of users. Copy the emailed token into {{companyInviteToken}}.

item.description: Firm manages its companies (clients) and their portal users. NEW this phase.

item.name: 9. QuickBooks (firm console)

exec: console.log('Open this in a browser to connect QuickBooks:\n' + d.authorizationUrl);

request.description: Owner/Admin only. Returns { authorizationUrl }. Open that URL in a browser, sign in to QuickBooks (a sandbox company while testing), pick ONE company and authorize. Intuit redirects to the callback, which auto-creates the company on the platform.

Public endpoint. You normally do NOT call this from Postman — Intuit's redirect hits it in the browser after the owner authorizes on the 'Add Company' URL. On success it 302-redirects to the firm console with ?quickbooks=connected&companyId=<id>; on failure with ?quickbooks=error&reason=<code>.
Returns a fresh { authorizationUrl } for an existing company. The owner re-authorizes the SAME QuickBooks company; the callback refreshes its tokens.

item.description: QuickBooks Online OAuth. A company is created by connecting QuickBooks: 'Add Company (start OAuth)' returns an authorizationUrl; the owner picks a company on Intuit; the public callback provisions it. 'Reconnect' refreshes an existing company's tokens; 'Disconnect' clears them; 'Connection status' reports the current state.

item.name: 10. QuickBooks Data (firm console)
item.description: Read-only access to the QuickBooks data Harava has mirrored for a company. Each entity has its own resource path (accounts, invoices, bills, …); GET /entities lists all slugs. Everything is scoped to {{companyId}} within the caller's tenant.

item.name: 11. Client Portal (company user)

request.description: Company user accepts their invite and is signed in with ROLE_CLIENT, scoped to one company.

item.description: The client portal. Company is taken from the token; a user only ever sees their own company.

item.name: 12. Reference data
item.description: Standard code sets for dropdowns (time zones, countries with their default currency, currencies). Any authenticated user.

item.name: 13. Client Dashboard (firm console)
item.description: Pre-aggregated financial insights per widget, computed live from the mirrored QuickBooks data. Scoped to {{companyId}}.

item.name: 14. QuickBooks Reports (firm console)
item.description: QuickBooks' own reports (authoritative, penny-exact). Common ones refresh on a schedule; the rest are fetched on-demand and cached. GET /dashboard/reports/{slug}.

item.name: 15. Notifications (in-app + push)

request.description: Register (or refresh) this user's FCM device token. Idempotent per token. platform is ANDROID | IOS | WEB. Captures the new device id into {{deviceId}}. With FCM disabled the token is stored but nothing is delivered.
All devices registered for the current user.
Remove a device (call on logout). 204 No Content.
The feed behind the bell, newest first. Set unread=true for unread-only. Captures the first notification id into {{notificationId}}.
Returns { unread: N } for the bell badge.
Mark a single notification read. 204 No Content.
Mark every notification read. Returns { marked: N }.

Firm broadcasts to a client company's portal users (audience=COMPANY + companyId) or to all firm staff (audience=ALL_STAFF, omit companyId). Accepted (202); the fan-out job materializes per-user feed rows. Captures {{broadcastId}}.

Platform admin broadcasts to every tenant (audience=ALL_TENANTS) or a chosen set (audience=TENANTS + tenantIds:["{{tenantId}}"]). Accepted (202); cross-tenant fan-out runs in the background. Captures {{broadcastId}}.
Same endpoint, authenticated as a client-portal user ({{clientToken}}). Use this to test that company users receive their own notifications.
The portal user's own feed — e.g. broadcasts sent to their company, or future review/approval notifications.

item.description:
In-app notification feed (the app's bell) plus device registration for optional FCM push, and the broadcast senders.

The feed and device endpoints work for ANY authenticated user. These requests use the firm-staff token {{token}}; to test as a company/portal user, swap {{token}} for {{clientToken}} (two ready-made client-portal variants are included at the bottom).

To see notifications appear: send a broadcast (or trigger the automated welcome by verifying an email), then call 'List my notifications' as a recipient. Push (FCM) is optional and off by default (FCM_ENABLED=false) — the feed works without it.

item.name: 16. Financial News

request.description: Business + health + general news for the caller's company country. country and category are shown as optional params (disabled by default) — enable them in the Params tab to scope explicitly; otherwise the company/tenant country and default categories apply.
Narrow to business news.
Narrow to health/healthcare news.
Comma-separate multiple categories.
Force a market, e.g. set {{newsCountry}} to ng, us, gb, za.
Firm user: news for a specific client company's country (from its QuickBooks CompanyInfo).
As a client-portal user ({{clientToken}}) — scoped to their company's country.
Full-text keyword search (NewsData q). Country defaults to the caller's company country; categories default to business,health,top. Supports AND/OR/NOT and quoted phrases.
Search with explicit country and category always applied.

item.description:
Company-aware news feed: business, health & general (top) news. Any authenticated user. The feed follows the CLIENT COMPANY's country, not the firm — a US firm managing a Nigerian company sees Nigerian news for it. Default categories are business,health,top; pass ?category= to narrow. ?country= overrides the country; firm users pass ?companyId= to target a client.

With NEWS_ENABLED=false these return placeholder headlines. The dev key is already set in .env (NEWS_ENABLED=true), so these return live news. Cached per country+categories in Redis. Also visible in Swagger UI under 'Financial news'.

exec: // Harava DPoP — attaches a signed proof-of-possession header to every request.
// Postman sandboxes have no Node 'crypto', so we use jsrsasign (pure JS, ECDSA + JWS).
// The library is fetched once and cached; signing happens even on the first request
// (it runs inside the load callback, which Postman waits for).
// jsrsasign's RNG seeding references browser globals — stub them for the sandbox.
eval(libSrc); // defines KJUR, KEYUTIL, hextob64u in this scope
// 1. One persistent EC P-256 key pair (cached as collection variables).
jwk = { crv: 'P-256', kty: 'EC', x: pj.x, y: pj.y };
// 2. Build the proof for this request.
var payload = { htm: pm.request.method.toUpperCase(), htu: htu,
// 3. Bind to the access token via `ath` when this request sends a Bearer token.
var header = { alg: 'ES256', typ: 'dpop+jwt', jwk: jwk };
var proof = KJUR.jws.JWS.sign(null, JSON.stringify(header), JSON.stringify(payload), prvKey);
console.log('DPoP: proof attached for ' + payload.htm + ' ' + htu);
console.error('DPoP: failed to build proof —', e);
if (err || !res) { console.error('DPoP: could not load jsrsasign —', err); return; }

variable.description: Matches APP_BASE_URL in .env. lvh.me resolves to 127.0.0.1. Platform admin works on this host directly; for tenant login by subdomain use http://<tenantSubdomain>.lvh.me:8080 or send the X-Tenant-ID header. (http://localhost:8080 also works for non-subdomain calls.)
Tenant billing mode sent when provisioning: SUBSCRIPTION (subject to paid billing, the API default) or OPEN (not billed).
Owner invitation token from the email.
Tenant access token (set automatically on login/accept).
Company-user invitation token from the email.
Auto-generated DPoP private key (PKCS#8 PEM). Leave blank; the pre-request script fills it once. Clear it to rotate to a new key.
Auto-generated DPoP public key (JWK). Leave blank; set automatically alongside the private key.
Cached jsrsasign library source (loaded from CDN on the first request). Leave blank; clear it to force a reload.
Set automatically by 'Add Company (start OAuth)'; open it in a browser.
A device registration token. Any string works while FCM is disabled; use a real FCM token to test live push.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the 'country override' news request (e.g. ng, us, gb, za).
Keyword(s) for the news search endpoint. Supports AND/OR/NOT and quoted phrases.
